source_row.rationale: The Institute for Healthcare Improvement defines PDSA as Plan, Do, Study, Act. Option C is correct. The cycle is an iterative method for testing a change, studying what happened, and deciding how to adapt the next cycle. Options A, B, and D substitute terms that are not part of the standard PDSA sequence.
source_row.source_detail: Institute for Healthcare Improvement — Model for Improvement, Testing Changes: PDSA is Plan, Do, Study, Act; PDSA cycles are iterative tests of change used to learn from results and adapt subsequent cycles. Current IHI Model for Improvement resource live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCLEX relevance independently verified against the 2026 NCSBN Management of Care performance-improvement activities. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: continuity/transfer of care, collaboration, legal/regulatory scope, quality improvement, leadership and professional-practice activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A unit uses the PDSA cycle to test a small practice change before wider implementation. What does PDSA stand for?
